title: Recurring Primitive Parameter Clumps
pattern: Multiple functions repeatedly pass the components of one domain concept (such as connection settings, a start/end date range, or a coordinate pair) as independent primitive arguments instead of representing the concept with a cohesive type.
why_bad: Signature and call-site changes must be synchronized across every function when the concept expands (e.g., adding a connection timeout), long parameter lists obscure intent, same-typed arguments such as start and end can be silently swapped, and cross-field validation rules (e.g., `end_date >= start_date`) have no natural owner. It indicates that a hidden struct is waiting to be extracted.
detection: Case 1 (data clump): identical clusters of three or more parameters with corresponding names and types recur across multiple distinct function signatures. Case 2 (primitive pair/range): a recurring sequence of primitives, including a pair such as start/end or a meaningful coordinate pair, carries shared domain meaning or validation rules and is passed together through multiple functions. Require semantic cohesion in either case; coincidentally matching primitive types are insufficient.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. Functions that happen to take similar primitives with no shared semantic relationship (e.g., `(user_id: u32, timeout: u32)`). Highly generic APIs or mathematics libraries where coordinates `(x, y, z)` are passed together but represent independent primitives with no shared domain behavior or invariant that warrants an object.
source: *Martin Fowler - Refactoring (1999)*, Chapter 3, "Data Clumps"; *Steve McConnell - Code Complete (2004)*, Chapter 13; *Martin Fowler - Refactoring, Chapter 10, "Introduce Parameter Object"*
